MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Sex: Male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Targeted testing for familial likely pathogenic COL4A5 mutation. Family history of condition consistent with Alport syndrome. Grandfather carries likely causative COL4A5 mutation (c.919G>A; p.Gly307Ser) in exon 16.

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Male patient, grandson of individual with known COL4A5 mutation. No reported haematuria.

METHODOLOGY
Targeted DNA sequencing of COL4A5 gene exon 16
Sample type: Peripheral blood (EDTA)
DNA extraction: QIAamp DNA Blood Mini Kit
PCR amplification: Custom primers flanking exon 16 of COL4A5
Sequencing: Bidirectional Sanger sequencing
Analysis software: Mutation Surveyor v5.1
Reference sequence: NM_000495.5 (COL4A5)

RESULTS
COL4A5 gene analysis:
Targeted testing for c.919G>A (p.Gly307Ser) variant in exon 16: NOT DETECTED

The familial likely pathogenic variant c.919G>A (p.Gly307Ser) in exon 16 of the COL4A5 gene was not identified in this patient.

Quality metrics:
- DNA concentration: 45 ng/μL
- A260/A280 ratio: 1.85
- Sequence coverage: 100% of target region
- Phred quality score: >30 for all bases

SUMMARY AND INTERPRETATION
Targeted molecular testing for the familial COL4A5 mutation (c.919G>A; p.Gly307Ser) was performed. This variant was NOT DETECTED in the patient.

The COL4A5 gene is located on the X chromosome and encodes the alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen. Pathogenic variants in COL4A5 cause X-linked Alport syndrome, characterized by progressive hereditary nephritis, sensorineural hearing loss, and ocular abnormalities.

The absence of the familial variant indicates that this patient has not inherited the likely pathogenic COL4A5 mutation from the maternal lineage and is therefore not at increased risk for Alport syndrome associated with this specific variant.

FOLLOW-UP RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling to discuss implications of test results
2. No specific surveillance for Alport syndrome is indicated based on these results
3. Carrier and prenatal testing available for other family members if indicated
4. Clinical correlation recommended if symptoms develop

LIMITATIONS
- This test only examined the specific familial variant in exon 16
- Other regions of COL4A5 and other genes associated with Alport syndrome were not analyzed
- Rare variants below the detection threshold of Sanger sequencing may not be detected

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Report date: [redacted date]
